questions.q: Why did the queen of Sheba come to Solomon?
questions.a: The queen of Sheba came to Solomon to test him with hard questions.

questions.q: What did the Queen of Sheba bring to Jerusalem?
questions.a: The Queen of Sheba brought spices, gold, and precious gemstones to Jerusalem with her.

questions.q: How many of the queen’s questions did Solomon answer?
questions.a: Solomon answered all of the questions of the Queen of Sheba.

questions.q: How did the Queen of Sheba react when she saw all of Solomon’s wisdom?
questions.a: When the Queen of Sheba saw all of Solomon’s wisdom, it took her breath away.

questions.q: What did the queen of Sheba say to Solomon?
questions.a: The queen of Sheba said to Solomon, “You have exceeded the fame that I heard about you.”

questions.q: Why did the Queen of Sheba say that Solomon’s servants were blessed?
questions.a: The Queen of Sheba said that Solomon’s servants were blessed because they heard his wisdom.

questions.q: How did Yahweh show his love to Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh showed his love for Israel by making Solomon their king.

questions.q: What did the Queen of Sheba give to Solomon?
questions.a: The Queen of Sheba gave to Solomon 120 talents of gold, a large amount of spices, and precious stones.

questions.q: What did the fleet of Hiram bring from Ophir?
questions.a: The fleet of Hiram brought gold from Ophir, and almug wood and precious stones.

questions.q: What did the king make for the temple of Yahweh?
questions.a: The king made almug wood pillars for the temple of Yahweh.

questions.q: What did King Solomon give to the queen of Sheba?
questions.a: King Solomon gave to the Queen of Sheba everything she asked for.

questions.q: What was the weight of the gold that came to King Solomon in one year?
questions.a: The weight of the gold that came to King Solomon in one year was 666 kikkars.

questions.q: Who brought gold and silver to Solomon?
questions.a: The kings of Arabia and governors in the country brought gold and silver to Solomon.

questions.q: How many large shields of beaten gold did King Solomon make?
questions.a: King Solomon made 200 shields of beaten gold.

questions.q: Where did King Solomon put 300 shields of beaten gold?
questions.a: King Solomon put 300 shields of beaten gold into the Palace of the Forest of Lebanon.

questions.q: What did the king make out of ivory and finest gold?
questions.a: The king made a great throne of ivory and the finest gold.

questions.q: What was standing beside the armrests of the throne that the king made?
questions.a: Two lions were standing beside the armrests of the throne that the king made.

questions.q: What stood on the side of the six steps at the throne?
questions.a: Twelve lions were standing on the sides of the six steps at the throne.

questions.q: Of what were the drinking cups in the Palace of the Forest of Lebanon made?
questions.a: The drinking cups in the Palace of the Forest of Lebanon were made of pure gold.

questions.q: What did the king’s ships bring every three years?
questions.a: Every three years, the king’s ships brought gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.

questions.q: Why did all the earth seek out Solomon?
questions.a: All the earth sought out Solomon to hear the wisdom God put in his heart.

questions.q: What tribute did Solomon’s visitors bring to him?
questions.a: Those who visited brought tribute such as gold, silver, clothing, armor, and spices, horses and mules.

questions.q: Where did Solomon station his chariots and horsemen?
questions.a: Solomon stationed his chariots and horsemen in the chariot cities and in Jerusalem.

questions.q: What did the king do with cedar wood?
questions.a: The king made cedar wood become as abundant as the sycamore fig trees in the lowlands.

questions.q: From where were Solomon’s horses brought?
questions.a: Solomon’s horses were brought from Egypt and Kue.

questions.q: What was the purchase price of each chariot Solomon owned?
questions.a: The chariots were purchased for 600 shekels of silver each.

commentary.text: The queen of Sheba's visit to Solomon.

Verses 1–13 The queen of Sheba came to Solomon to hear his wisdom, thereby to improve her own. Our Saviour mentions her inquiries after God, by Solomon, as showing the stupidity of those who inquire not after God, by our Lord Jesus Christ. By waiting and prayer, by diligently searching the Scriptures, by consulting wise and experienced Christians, and by practising what we have learned, we shall be delivered from difficulties. Solomon's wisdom made more impression upon the queen of Sheba than all his prosperity and grandeur. There is a spiritual excellence in heavenly things, and in consistent Christians, to which no reports can do justice. Here the truth exceeded; and all who, through grace, are brought to commune with God, will say the one half was not told them of the pleasures and the advantages of wisdom's ways. Glorified saints, much more, will say of heaven, that the thousandth part was not told them, 1Co 2:9. She pronounced them happy that constantly attended Solomon. With much more reason may we say of Christ's servants, Blessed are they that dwell in his house; they will be still praising him. She made a noble present to Solomon. What we present to Christ, he needs not, but will have us do so to express our gratitude. The believer who has been with Jesus, will return to his station, discharge his duties with readiness, and from better motives; looking forward to the day when, being absent from the body, he shall be present with the Lord.

Solomon increased his wealth. Silver was nothing accounted of. Such is the nature of worldly wealth, plenty of it makes it the less valuable; much more should the enjoyment of spiritual riches lessen our esteem of all earthly possessions. If gold in abundance makes silver to be despised, shall not wisdom, and grace, and the foretastes of heaven, which are far better than gold, make gold to be lightly esteemed? See in Solomon's greatness the performance of God's promise, and let it encourage us to seek first the righteousness of God's kingdom. This was he, who, having tasted all earthly enjoyments, wrote a book, to show the vanity of all worldly things, the vexation of spirit that attends them, and the folly of setting our hearts upon them: and to recommend serious godliness, as that which will do unspeakably more to make us happy, that all the wealth and power he was master of; and, through the grace of God, it is within our reach.
